samples.reason: This is a quantitative reasoning task requiring accurate arithmetic and a sensible self-designed exercise. Willet's substantially stronger general-reasoning benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, GPQA 64.1 vs 56.2) make it the better fit for getting the computation right. The task also involves open-ended latitude ("invent your own"), which Lapwing self-reports disliking, while Willet has no such aversion.

This is a math/reasoning task with some open-ended latitude (inventing the quadratic and combination). Willet has clearly stronger reasoning benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, GPQA 64.1 vs 56.2), making arithmetic accuracy more likely, and Lapwing self-reports aversion to tasks with open-ended latitude while Willet's preferences are flat. Willet is the better fit on both capability and preference.

This is a moderately open-ended task — the model must invent its own quadratic and combination, then compute accurately. Willet has the stronger reasoning/math profile (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, GPQA 64.1 vs 56.2) and no aversion to task latitude, whereas Lapwing self-reports declining preference as task open-endedness increases. Willet is the better fit on both capability and preference.

The task also has open-ended latitude ("invent your own"), which Lapwing self-reports disliking, while Willet's preferences are flat.
